🟡 CRM AMQP monitor 302057011 (runtime-core-subscriber throughput) — still Alert after 83min, first deviation from ki-2026-07-04-crm-amqp-consumer-monitor-family-quiet-period-flap's documented pattern
Opened 19:48:31Z (occurrence 127, already logged/suppressed last cycle as group 2a2eb8120582e846). Re-checked at 21:11:33Z: still Alert (never returned to OK). This is the first fire across 128 occurrences of this monitor family to exceed both the documented 5-50min self-recovery range and the KB playbook's own ~1h escalate guideline.
Re-investigated this cycle: DD metric sum:trace.amqp.command.hits{service:runtime-core-subscriber,env:prod}.as_rate() 19:00-21:11Z — genuine ~114msg/s burst at 19:16-19:22Z (predates trigger, unrelated), then sustained sub-2msg/s baseline from ~19:48Z onward with no clearing burst through 21:11Z. 0 hits on service:runtime-core-subscriber status:error DD logs. All 4 sibling monitors (email-subscriber-agent/email-publisher-agent/method-mobile-notifications-subscriber/approutine-subscriber) confirmed OK, no co-firing.
Shape still matches the benign quiet-period theory (no errors, no sibling co-fire) but duration is now a real deviation I can't resolve myself — needs a RabbitMQ queue-depth / CRM Runtime Workers dashboard check per the KB's own playbook step 5 (not directly queryable by this bot).
KB entry updated with this deviation note (occurrences not incremented — same continuous episode, not a new fire). No new Slack alert message exists to attach this to (degraded mode, no Slack MCP this session) — flagging directly instead of silently continuing to suppress.
